sources.title: Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) (web.dev)
findings: Layout shifts within 500 ms of a discrete user input (tap, click, keypress) carry hadRecentInput and are excluded; scrolls and drags are not recent input.
When an interaction starts a slow request, reserve space and show a loading indicator right away so content does not move when the result arrives.
sources.limits: Chrome team guidance; the metric is defined by the Layout Instability spec.

sources.title: Every Layout: Boxes (Heydon Pickering, Andy Bell)
findings: By default a box's size is its content plus padding and border (content-box); border-box makes the declared width include padding and border and is preferable for all boxes.
Apply box-sizing: border-box to all elements with the universal selector.

sources.title: Every Layout: The Stack (Heydon Pickering, Andy Bell)
findings: Components designed in isolation should not carry the margin that separates them; style the context instead.
The Stack injects margin between siblings from their common parent (.stack > * + * with margin-block-start), leaving no stray margin.

sources.title: Inclusive Components: Toggle Buttons (Heydon Pickering)
findings: A true toggle button is a button element with aria-pressed; its label names what is toggled and styles hook onto [aria-pressed].
Never change the pressed state and the label together; a label that flips between play and pause is a state change no assistive technology announces.
sources.limits: Practitioner pattern library; the book edition updates the examples.

sources.title: Inclusive Components: Menus and Menu Buttons (Heydon Pickering)
findings: The ARIA menu and menuitem roles are for application menus; a site navigation of links should not use them, because menuitem overrides the link role and is not meant to contain interactive descendants.

sources.title: CUBE CSS (Andy Bell)
findings: CUBE stands for Composition, Utility, Block, Exception: a methodology that extends the cascade rather than working against it, unlike approaches such as BEM.
sources.limits: The author calls the documentation a work in progress.

sources.title: CUBE CSS: Composition (Andy Bell)
findings: The composition layer provides high-level flexible layouts, decides how elements interact, and creates flow and rhythm (for example .flow > * + * with a margin token).
It does not provide visual treatment (color, font style), decoration, or force a pixel-perfect layout.

sources.title: CUBE CSS: Exception (Andy Bell)
findings: An exception is a deviation from a block's rules, such as a reversed or inactive state, expressed with a data attribute (data-state) that serves as a hook for both CSS and JavaScript.

sources.title: HTML: A good basis for accessibility (MDN)
findings: Use semantic controls (button, a, form elements) where possible; a div button needs tabindex, a role, and key handling added back by hand.
Positive tabindex values for a custom tab order are nearly always a bad idea because they confuse the order.

sources.title: ARIA (MDN)
findings: Prefer the semantic HTML element over ARIA; the first rule of ARIA is to use a native element or attribute that has the semantics and behavior built in.
With ARIA you must reproduce the browser behavior in script; WebAIM found home pages with ARIA averaged 41 percent more detected errors.

sources.title: Progressive enhancement (MDN Glossary)
findings: Progressive enhancement delivers a baseline of essential content and functionality to as many users as possible and layers richer behavior on capable browsers, using feature detection.

sources.title: CSS logical properties and values (MDN)
findings: Logical properties map layout to the writing direction (block and inline, start and end) instead of physical left, right, top, and bottom, so content in right-to-left or vertical writing modes renders as intended.

sources.title: Cascade layers (MDN Learn)
findings: For normal declarations later layers beat earlier ones and unlayered styles beat all layers; for !important the order reverses.
Layer order, set once, decides precedence before specificity does.

sources.title: <dialog>: The Dialog element (MDN)
findings: Baseline widely available since March 2022; showModal() opens a modal dialog, moves focus to the first focusable element (or the autofocus target), and closes on Escape.
Provide an explicit close button; keyboard users expect Escape to close modal dialogs.

sources.title: Specificity (MDN)
findings: Specificity is the weight the cascade uses to pick the most relevant declaration; the page gives tips for avoiding and overriding !important, including isolating unavoidable overrides in a first imported layer.
